source: Mandara MP, Mhalu FS - Cholera control in an inaccessible district in Tanzania (Med J Zambia 1980;15(1):10-13)
processing_notes: Source states: 'The fourth ever recorded outbreak of cholera on Tanzania mainland started on 2.10.77 in Twasalie village which is a delta island in the Utete district on the Indian Ocean coastal line ... Whereas 55% of the 69 patients with the disease before control measures were introduced died, the mortality rate was reduced to 1.6% out of the 184 severely ill patients admitted to treatment centres.' - interpreted as 253 sCh cases, 41 deaths. Cases derived by addition of the two explicitly stated patient groups: 69 patients before control measures + 184 severely ill patients admitted to treatment centres = 253. Deaths derived from the two stated mortality percentages: 0.55*69 = 38 plus 0.016*184 = 3, total 41 (CFR 16.2%). Both are arithmetic conversions of quoted figures, not source-stated totals - confidence capped accordingly. Location: Utete District is the historical name of present-day Rufiji District, Pwani Region (Twasalie village, Rufiji delta island). TR is bounded at 1977-12-31 because the source gives no end date; the WHO WER 1977 annual table reports 267 cases nationally for Tanzania (including 22 suspect) which is consistent with this outbreak accounting for essentially the whole 1977 national total, so the bulk of cases fell within 1977. District subset - do not sum with the national WHO annual row for 1977.

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in 1976 (WER 1977, 52, No. 19, pp. 165-167)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1975-01-01..1976-12-31. Source states: 'Table 1. Cases of Cholera Notified to WHO, 1976 - AFRICA: Benin 146, Cape Verde 219, Comoros 5, Ghana 2, Kenya 1359, Liberia 646, Malawi 19, Morocco 2, Nigeria 34, Southern Rhodesia 144, United Republic of Cameroon 135, TOTAL 2711. No new territory was affected during the year.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Tanzania is absent from the WHO WER notification table for BOTH 1976 (11 African countries listed above) and 1975 (WER 1976, 51, No. 18: 14 African countries listed - Algeria, Angola, Benin, Cape Verde, Comoros, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Mozambique, Nigeria, Southern Rhodesia, Uganda, United Republic of Cameroon, Upper Volta). Both land neighbours Kenya and Uganda appear in those tables, so the tables do cover East Africa. Tanzania notified 10 cases in 1974 and 267 in 1977, i.e. the national notification channel to WHO was functioning either side of this window, which distinguishes this from a reporting blackout. Resolution of the 'fourth ever recorded outbreak' question: Mandara and Mhalu (Med J Zambia 1980) place outbreak #4 at Rufiji from 2 Oct 1977 with about 253 cases; the WER 1977 national total is 267, leaving roughly 14 cases for earlier 1977 foci - consistent with outbreaks #2 and #3 being small early-1977 events rather than unreported 1975/1976 epidemics. Surveillance recorded as partial: detection sensitivity in this era was low (only 10 cases detected in 1974), so a small undetected focus cannot be excluded; confidence set to 0.85 rather than 1.0 for that reason.

source: PLOS NTD - Genomic insights into Vibrio cholerae O1 responsible for cholera epidemics in Tanzania between 1993 and 2017 (PMC6927581)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2014-01-01..2014-12-31. Source states: 'V. cholerae O1 strains from 2013 were not available and there was no cholera reported in Tanzania in 2014.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Triangulated with two independent WHO-derived sources: (1) the WHO Global Health Observatory annual cholera series for Tanzania (indicators CHOLERA_0000000001/2/3, queried directly via the GHO OData API) contains rows for every year 1977-2013 and 2015-2016 but NO row for 2014, i.e. Tanzania made no 2014 cholera notification while the notification channel was demonstrably working either side of it (270 cases in 2013, 11 563 in 2015); (2) the JHU baseline file data/TZA/cholera_data_jhu.csv carries a weekly row 2014-12-29..2015-01-04 with 0 cases. Surveillance recorded as operational: Tanzania's IDSR detected and reported the January 2015 Kigoma outbreak (JHU week 2015-01-12..2015-01-18, 361 cases) within weeks of onset. A candidate counter-claim of a November 2014 Morogoro/Mvomero outbreak was checked against the cited Swahili source (michuzi.co.tz, 22 December 2015) and that article contains no 2014 or Morogoro reference - the lead did not hold. Caveat: the source phrase is 'no cholera reported', which is a notification statement; sub-threshold undetected transmission cannot be formally excluded, hence confidence 0.85 rather than 1.0.
